import pytest
from your_module import snake_to_camel  # Replace with actual module name

class TestSnakeToCamel:
    """Unit tests for snake_to_camel function."""

    # --- Happy Path ---
    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "input_str, expected",
        [
            ("hello_world", "helloWorld"),
            ("snake_to_camel", "snakeToCamel"),
            ("a_b_c", "aBC"),
            ("hello_world_foo", "helloWorldFoo"),
            ("hello_123_world", "hello123World"),
            ("hello_world_123", "helloWorld123"),
            ("alreadyCamel", "alreadyCamel"),
            ("Hello_World", "HelloWorld"),
            ("_hello", "Hello"),          # leading underscore
            ("hello_", "hello"),          # trailing underscore
            ("hello__world", "helloWorld"), # double underscore
            ("__hello", "Hello"),         # multiple leading underscores
            ("hello__", "hello"),         # multiple trailing underscores
            ("___", ""),                  # only underscores
            ("", ""),                     # empty string
            ("single", "single"),         # single word
        ],
    )
    def test_snake_to_camel(self, input_str, expected):
        """Test typical and edge-case conversions."""
        assert snake_to_camel(input_str) == expected

    # --- Error Cases ---
    def test_snake_to_camel_none_input(self):
        """Test that passing None raises AttributeError."""
        with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
            snake_to_camel(None)

    def test_snake_to_camel_int_input(self):
        """Test that passing an integer raises AttributeError."""
        with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
            snake_to_camel(123)

    def test_snake_to_camel_list_input(self):
        """Test that passing a list raises AttributeError."""
        with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
            snake_to_camel(["hello", "world"])
